label: Delimiter step, biased by long sequences and by first/second original token in {s,m,x,p,t,i,1,d}
explanation: About 61% of activation mass falls on the <DEL> step, and it is active on 32% of delimiter steps. Whether it fires there depends on the sequence content: it fires much more when L is 8-9 and when the first original token (the one output at <DEL>) or the second one (the next output) is in {s,m,x,p,t,i,1,d}. The largest activations are at <DEL> in long sequences that start with s/m/x/t/1. The other ~35% of mass falls on the original phase from t>=3, mostly on the first occurrence of a token (in_first) and most often for inputs 3, c, e, k, b. These activations ramp up toward the delimiter and are not covered by the predicate. It almost never fires in the copy phase after recall_idx 4, and never at t=0-1. The effect looks like a graded, distributed code of sequence contents, not a clean rule. Dev scores: F1 0.47, mass recall 0.60. phase==1 alone gives F1 0.39 and mass recall 0.61.
